children: Microsoft, the cloud and enterprise-software group

, targets more AI output from each megawatt with its next-generation Maia system, while shares traded at $540.41, down approximately 0.56% at 10.25am EST, on October 14. The company expects Maia 300 to produce 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems. That implies roughly 28.6% less power for the same output, provided workloads and performance requirements are comparable. The valuation chart places the stock 8.83% below its $592.76 GF Value estimate, suggesting a modest valuation cushion.

The hardware push has a timetable. The Register reported that Maia 300 production deployments are scheduled for 2027. Microsoft's October 12 announcement details racks with 96 accelerators, 27.6 terabytes of high-bandwidth memory and a 167-kilowatt power envelope. Maia 200 already handles production workloads, including Copilot. Starting in 2027, Microsoft plans to expand Maia toward multi-gigawatt deployments and make it the main inference infrastructure for its products and services.

For investors, the test is whether that efficiency reaches the income statement. More tokens per megawatt could stretch available power capacity, but it does not establish a margin gain. Hardware costs, utilization, software spending and facility overhead still matter. Watch deployment progress and operating results under comparable workload quality and latency. Serving more revenue-generating AI demand from each unit of power would make the spending case stronger.

title: Microsoft Stocks Slip Lower Although Maia Targets 40% More Tokens per Megawatt
